sets.relationshipLabel: a tool and the exact action it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A chisel exists to carve just as a lathe exists to turn — each tool is defined by its one signature motion.

sets.relationshipLabel: an object placed to stop the mark it would otherwise cause
sets.explanation: A coaster exists to stop a stain and a felt pad exists to stop a scratch — both are small guards against damage from the object they sit under.
baitTags: object-mark pairing could be mistaken for tool-action

sets.relationshipLabel: a surface that conceals the cheaper or structural material beneath it
sets.explanation: Veneer hides particleboard and upholstery hides a frame — both are the visible skin covering the cheaper structure underneath.
baitTags: upholstery/frame could look like a synonym pair for furniture parts

sets.relationshipLabel: an older, specific name for the same everyday furniture piece
sets.explanation: A davenport is an old-fashioned word for a sofa, and a hassock is an old-fashioned word for an ottoman — each pair names the same object across generations.
baitTags: dated vocabulary reads as unrelated furniture terms at first
